title: Allow more homes near jobs and transport
action: Change zoning so more homes, including townhouses and mid-rise apartments, can be built in established areas close to jobs, transport and services, with housing targets backed by evidence.
why: Restrictive zoning in well-located suburbs pushes new homes to the urban fringe, far from jobs. That raises housing costs, lengthens commutes and limits which jobs people can take, lowering productivity.

evidence.source: Building more homes where people want to live
evidence.quote: To address this shortage, the state should prioritise increasing housing supply where households want to live.

evidence.source: NSW Productivity Commission White Paper 2021: Rebooting the economy
evidence.quote: Develop and implement a system of long-term housing targets underpinned by strong evidence and governance.

precedents.what: Allowed mid-rise housing near designated railway stations from 2024.

tradeoffs: More density needs matching infrastructure; the cost is lower in established areas than on the fringe.
